Course Description: An introduction to fluid mechanics and heat transfer. column2: Course Description: Overview of the finite element method (FEM) and its use to solve general problems in 2-D and 3-D. Course Description: The aim of the course is to develop and practice the interdisciplinary skills required to solve open-ended engineering design problems from a mechatronics perspective. Students will experience all phases of the design process, including: problem definition, generation and evaluation of concepts, engineering analysis and testing, and preparation of design documentation. Project management and communications skills will also be emphasized. A faculty advisor will supervise project teams and an interdisciplinary committee comprised of Mechatronics program faculty members will assess project outcomes. Antirequisite(s): CBE 4497, the former MME 4419, CEE 4441, GPE 4497, SE 4450, MME 4499, ECE 4415, ECE 4416, Engineering Science 4499. Extra Information: 6 laboratory/project hours. Restricted to students enrolled in the Mechatronic Systems Engineering program.
